0

Introduction

4

Definitions

IS0 8860 specifies the characteristics of 90 mm (3.5 in) flexible disk cartridges recorded at 7 968 ftprad using modified frequency modulation (MFM) recording on 80 tracks on each side. IS0 8860-2 specifies the track layout, the track format and the characteristics of the recorded signals. IS0 8860-l and IS0 8860-2, together with the labelling scheme specified in IS0 9293, provide for full data interchange between data processing systems.

For the purpose of this International Standard the following definitions apply. 4.1 recording disk : A flexible disk which accepts and retains, on the specified side or sides, magnetic signals intended for input/output and storage purposes. 4.2 hub : A centring and referencing device attached to the centre of the disk which allows torque to be transmitted to the disk. It ensures centring of the disk on the drive shaft in a unique angular position. 4.3 shutter : A device which uncovers the head windows upon insertion, and automatically covers them upon removal from the drive. 4.4 liner : Suitable material positioned between the case and the disk to provide cleaning action and protection from abrasion. 4.5 case : A protecrive enclosure mechanism and a write-inhibit hole. including a shutter

1

Scope

and field

of application

This part of IS0 8866 specifies the dimensional, physical and magnetic characteristics of the cartridge, so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems.
NOTE - Numeric values in the SI and/or Imperial measurements system in this part of IS.0 8860 may have been rounded off and therefore are consistent with, but not exactly equal to, each other. Either system may be used, but the two should be neither intermixed norreconverted. The original design was made using SI units.

2

Conformance

A 90 mm (3.5 in) flexible disk cartridge shall be in conformance with this part of IS0 8860 if it meets all mandatory requirements contained herein.

4;6 Master Standard Reference Flexible Disk Cartridge : A reference flexible disk cartridge selected as the standard for reference fields, signal amplitudes, resolution, peak shift and overwrite. Track 00 and track 79 on both sides are declared as reference tracks. The reference tracks are calibrated at 600 r/min. The calibration is also valid at 300 r/min.

4.8 Typical Field : In the plot of average signal amplitude against recording field at the specified track and flux transition density, the Typical Field is the minimum field which causes a signal output equal to 95 % of the maximum Average Signal Amplitude.

4.11 Standard Reference Amplitudes BRAS) : The Average Signal Amplitudes derived from the reference tracks of the Master Standard' Reference Flexible Disk Cartridge using the Test Recording Current. There are four SRAs, two for each side. SRAlf is the Average Signal Amplitude from a recording written using Test Frequency lfat Track 00. elements

The main elements of the flexible disk cartridge are the recording disk; the liner, the case. Description

.

5.3

4.12 Average Signal Amplitude : For a track : the arithmetically averaged value of the output voltages measured peak-to-peak over the whole track.

The cartridge is of a substantially square form. It includes a central hole on one side, a heat window on both sides and a write-inhibit hole. The liner is provided between the case and the disk. It comprises two layers of material between which the disk lies. The disk has a central hole with a metal hub attached.

4.13 in-contact : An operating condition in which the magnetic surface of the disk is in physical contact with the magnetic heads.

6.1.3

Storage

environment

7
During storage the cartridges shall be kept under the following conditions : temperature

Dimensional

characteristics

: 4 to 53 OC (39 to 127 OFI : 8 to 90 %

The dimensions of the cartridge are referred to two reference axes X and Y, i.e. two lines in space intersecting at right angles. The plane they define is the Reference Plane XY of the cartridge.

relative humidity

There shall be no deposit of moisture on or in the cartridge. The ambient stray magnetic field shall not exceed 4 000 A/m (50 Oe).
NOTE - Cartridges which have been stored at temperatures and humidities exceeding the operating conditions may exhibit degraded performance characteristics. Such cartridges should be subjected to a conditioning period of not less than 24 h within the operating environment prior to use.

The write-inhibit hole is intended for use either with a mechanical switch or with an optical detector so that only when the hole is covered is writing on the disk possible. Also when covered, the,light transmittance of the write-inhibit hole area shall not exceed 1 %, when measured with an optical system as described in annex B.

Physical

characteristics

Inflammability

The disk, case and liner components shall be made from materials that, if ignited from a match flame, do not continue to burn in a still carbon dioxide atmosphere.

9:3

Functional

testing

For the purpose of the following tests the same drive unit shall be used for writing and reading operations, both for the disk under test and for the Master Standard Reference Flexible Disk Cartridge. The in-contact condition shall be used.

9.2
9.2.1

Track geometry
9.3.1 Number of tracks

Surface tests

In the recording area there shall be 80 discrete concentric tracks on each side of the disk. The distance between centrelines of adjacent tracks shall be 0,187 5 mm (0.007 38 in). The resulting track density is 5.33 tpmm (135.467 tpi). 9.2.2 Width of tracks

9.9.1.4

Resolution

`After recording'on track 79, using the Test Recording Current, the ratio Average Signal Amplitude using 2f Average Signal Amplitude using lf shall be greater than 80 % of the same ratio for the Master Standard Reference Flexible Disk Cartridge. This test shall be performed on both sides. 9.3.1.5 Peak shift

On b$h sides, on rmck 00 using lf and on track 79 using 2f. modulation shall be kss than 10 %. 9.3.2 Track quality tests

These tests shall apply to all 60 tracks at the defined positions on each side. The Test Recording Current shall be used.

9.39.1

Missing pulse

The average peak shift measured on the diskcartridge under test, using the method specified in annex E, shall be within the range from 63 % to 137 % of that of the Master Standard Reference Flexible Disk Cartridge. This test shall be performed for both sides on track 79. 9.3.1.6 Overwrite

Write a track at 2fwith the appropriate Test Recording Current. Any playback signal which, when measured base-to-@eak, is less than 45 % of half the arithmetically averaged value of the output voltages measured peak-to-peak over the whole track, shall be a missing pulse.

9.3.2.2

Extra pulse

On track 00 after recording with the Test Recording Current, first using ?ffor one revolution andthen overwriting with 2ffor one revolution, the ratio Residual Average Signal Amplitude at lf after overwrite using 2s Average Signal Amplitude after first recording using lf shall be less than 125 % of the value of the same ratio for the Master Standard Reference Fletiible Disk Cartridge. This test shall be'performed on both sides, and a frequency-selective voltmeter with a bandwidth of 1 kliz to 5 ktiz shall be used. 9.3.1.7 Modulation

Write a track at 2J Erase the track for one'revolution with a direct current equivalent to the quiescent value of the Test Recording Current. Any playback signal which, when measured base-to-peak, exceeds 20 % of half the Average Signal Amplitude at 2Jof the track under test shall be an extra pulse. 9.3.3 9.3.3.1 Rejection criterion Defective track

A track on which one or more missing or extra pulses, or both, are detected in the same position(s) on consecutive passes shall be a defective track: The applicable'number of consecutive passes shall be a matter for agreement between the interested parties.

Modulation shall be Maximum mean Minimum mean 9.3.3.2 x 100% As initially received from the medium supplier, the cartridge shall have no defective tracks. Requirement for tracks

Maximum mean t- MInimum mean

The maximum mean shall be the average value of the amplitude modulated output voltage in that part of the track with the maximum amplitudes; and the minimum mean shall be that in the respective part with the minimum amplitudes. Output voltage shall be measured peak-to-peak; averaging shall be done over about 2 000 consecutive flux transitions.

9.3.3.3

Rejected cartridge

A cartridge which does not meet the requirements of 9.3.3.2 shall be rejected. I

Test for compliance

A.1

The purpose of this test is to determine whether the cartridge will maintain the proper plane of operation within the drive. This is achieved by supporting the cartridge at defined reference zones and applying forces opposite to the supports.

Annex B Measurement of light transmittance

(This annex forms part of the standard.)

B.l

Introduction

The following description outlines the general principle of the measuring equipmvt and the measuring method to be applied when measuring the radiation (light) transmittance of the writeinhibit hole and the opacity of its cover. For the purpose of this part of IS0 9950 "light transmittance" is defined by convention as the relationship between the reading obtained from the test device with the sample inserted and the reading obtained when no samble is present. The transmittance value is expressed as the percentage ratio of the two readings. The essential elements of the measuring equipment are

a is the angle where the relative intensity of the LED is equal to, or greater than, 95 % of the maximum intensity in the optical axis. The aperture shall have a thickness of 1.2 to 1.4 mm and a diameter given by D = C&C, tana) mm L2 = K, + 1.5) mm

Its surfaces shall be matt black. The whole device should be enclosed within a light-tight casing.

Annex Method for measuring

C track width

the effective

(This annex forms part of the standard.)

Erase a 7-track wide band. Record a 250 000 ftps frequency pattern in a track centred in the middle of the erased band, with the read/write head with the erase element active. Measure the output voltage.

back signal amplitude for each incremental move and plot its amplitude versus displacement, See figure 11 for reading the half track width A and B for both sides of displacement, provided the gap width of the head used is not smaller than the effective track width. The total effective track width is the sum of A and B. Repeat the test to ensure that no thermal or hygroscopic effects have taken place during the measurement.

Move the head radially over the disk in increments not greater than 0,010 mm fO.000 4 in) to the left and to the right until the read back signal has decreased by 75 %. Determine the read

Annex Method

E peak shift
1

for measuring

(This annex forms part of the standard.

El

Introduction

The resolution of a flexible disk system ,at the inner tracks, where the recording density is highest, shall be sufficiently high to minimize peak shift. However, it shall not be too high at the outer tracks, where the recording density is lowest, otherwise spurious read signals may be generated. This test determines the characteristics of the disk by measuring the peak shift at inner tracks and setting limits for the upper and lower values.

It is terminated by the trailing edge of the first output pulse of the LS 221 timer to occur during the period of the next index pulse timer. output Waveform e) is passed to the time interval counter during the sampling period.

E.2.3

Period of the LS 221 timer

The period of the LS 221 timer shall be 3 us when testing at 606 r/min;

E.2 E.2.1

bescription

of the measuring

equipment

6 us when testing at 300 r/min. E.2.4

Peak shift test drive

Time interval

counter

The drive shall be any drive suitable for use at 7 95B ftprad.

The counter shall have a resolution of 5 ns or better.

E.,2.2

Peak shift measurement

circuit

The measurement circuit shall be as shown in figure 13 The operation of the circuit is illustrated in the timing diagram (see figure 14) as follows : a) index pulse b) index pulse timer A 1 ms timer triggered by the index pulse. Its output masks the discontinuities that occur in the recording when the write current is switched off.

E.3
E.3.1

Method

of test

AC bulk-erase the disk cartridge under test.

E.3.2 Using the Test Recording Current, write the test pattern DB6 t110110110110...) continuously on track 79 on each side, commencing with the index pulse and switching off the write current when the index pulse is detected at the end of one revolution.

E.3.3 Read back on the same test drive and measure intervals T" on the time interval counter.
NOTE - To minimizeerrors due to changes in the rotationalspeed of the drive, it is essentialthat reading occurs immediately after writing.

c) read signal
The read signal resulting from the test pattern. The positive-going edge of the first bit of a pair triggers the LS 74 flip-flop. The negative-going edge of the first bit of a pair triggers the LS 221 timer. d) bit period window This is the output waveform of the LS 221 timer. It allows the positive-going edge of the second bit of a pair to reset flip-flop LS 74. e) is the output of the LS 74; its duration is the time interval T" between the two bits of a pair, f) sampling period This period commences when the second LS 74 flip-flop is set by the trailing edge of d) after the index pulse timer has reset.

E.3.4

Sampling

Method

E.3.4.1 The data recording area extends from the leading edge of the index pulse to the leading edge of the next index pulse. E.3.4.2 The sampling area extends from the resetting of the index pulse timer to the leading edge of the next index pulse [resulting from E.2.2 b)]. 5.X4.3 The preferred sampling method is to measure every 7" i*cterval in the sampling area, if permitted by the sampling rate of the time interval counter. If the sampling rate of the counter piohibits the measurement of every T', then a lesser number of T' measurements shall be permitted, providing that the sampiing is random.
